title: (Updated) Microsoft PowerPoint: Review sales pipeline Copilot skill
summary: Microsoft PowerPoint is introducing a new Copilot skill, Review sales pipeline, to help users create or update sales pipeline and forecast presentations. The feature is rolling out worldwide from late October to late November 2026 on Windows, Mac, and web, requiring no admin action or changes to data handling.
body:
Updated November 3, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We are introducing a new Copilot skill in PowerPoint, Review sales pipeline, that helps users create or refresh internal pipeline and forecast review presentations focused on opportunity movement, risks, and next actions.

[Rollout schedule]

- General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout began late October 2026 and is expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously early November).[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

- Users with access to Copilot in PowerPoint.Platforms and services

- Microsoft PowerPoint for Windows (Win32), Mac, and web.- Copilot in PowerPoint.What will happen

- Users will be able to use a scenario-specific Copilot skill to create or refresh internal pipeline and forecast review presentation drafts.- The skill helps users review opportunities, pipeline movement, risks, and next actions for recurring sales management discussions.[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required. We recommend that you inform sales managers and PowerPoint Copilot users that this new skill is becoming available in PowerPoint on Windows (Win32), Mac, and web.

[Compliance considerations]

Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed (e.g., documents, emails, chats, etc.)?

- No. This update adds a scenario-specific authoring skill in PowerPoint and does not introduce new customer data storage or change existing Microsoft 365 data handling pipelines.Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?

- No. The change does not introduce a new AI system-of-record; it provides a new entry point/experience within existing Copilot in PowerPoint capabilities.Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?

- No. Users continue to interact through existing Copilot in PowerPoint experiences.
bodyHtml:
Updated November 3, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We are introducing a new Copilot skill in PowerPoint, Review sales pipeline, that helps users create or refresh internal pipeline and forecast review presentations focused on opportunity movement, risks, and next actions.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout began late October 2026 and is expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously early November).

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with access to Copilot in PowerPoint.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft PowerPoint for Windows (Win32), Mac, and web.
  • Copilot in PowerPoint.

What will happen

  • Users will be able to use a scenario-specific Copilot skill to create or refresh internal pipeline and forecast review presentation drafts.
  • The skill helps users review opportunities, pipeline movement, risks, and next actions for recurring sales management discussions.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required. We recommend that you inform sales managers and PowerPoint Copilot users that this new skill is becoming available in PowerPoint on Windows (Win32), Mac, and web.

[Compliance considerations]

Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed (e.g., documents, emails, chats, etc.)?

  • No. This update adds a scenario-specific authoring skill in PowerPoint and does not introduce new customer data storage or change existing Microsoft 365 data handling pipelines.

Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?

  • No. The change does not introduce a new AI system-of-record; it provides a new entry point/experience within existing Copilot in PowerPoint capabilities.

Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?

  • No. Users continue to interact through existing Copilot in PowerPoint experiences.
